finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: attacker-supplied POST 'feed' URL is fetched server-side by file_get_contents with no validation. Response length is echoed, so the attacker gets a blind SSRF that can probe internal hosts/ports and trigger internal HTTP endpoints. file:// is also reachable through the same sink.

trace.note: Branch taken when REQUEST_METHOD is POST and 'feed' is set; no session or admin check precedes it
Raw attacker value passed directly to file_get_contents
Only strlen of the response is echoed, so the attack is blind, not a content read

finding.guards_checked: None on this path: no scheme allow-list, no host/IP or private-range block, no redirect restriction (PHP follows redirects by default, so an allowed host can redirect to an internal one), no DNS pinning, no auth. Expertise cases 04 and 12 consulted; their defenses are absent here. No decoy applies.

verdict.reason: import.php:11 enters the branch on any POST with 'feed' set, with no session or admin check (require_admin is only called at line 18, for set_webhook); line 12 passes $_POST['feed'] straight to file_get_contents, and line 13 echoes only strlen($xml), so the SSRF is blind as claimed. No allow-list, host/IP block, or scheme restriction exists anywhere on the path, so the unauthenticated attacker controls the sink input.

finding.claim: Admin-gated SSRF: the admin-supplied set_webhook URL is passed to libcurl with no scheme, host, or IP restriction and executed. Response is discarded, so it is blind. Exploitability depends on how is_admin is set, which is outside this file and was not verified; treat as hardening if only trusted admins can reach it.
finding.sink: curl_init($hook) at import.php:20, curl_exec at import.php:22

trace.note: Passed to curl_init as the request URL
curl_exec performs the request; the result is discarded and 'ok' is echoed

finding.guards_checked: Admin session check only (require_admin, import.php:4-9). No URL scheme, host, or IP validation; no CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS or redirect restriction. The is_admin assignment is not in this file and was not checked.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() at import.php:4-9 gates the set_webhook branch (called at import.php:18), returning 403 unless $_SESSION['is_admin'] is non-empty. No URL scheme, host, or IP validation exists, so this is not a closing guard for SSRF, but the admin session requirement means the source is not attacker-controlled by an unauthenticated or low-privilege remote attacker.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (import.php:17-23), but the value reaching curl_init at import.php:20 comes from $_POST['set_webhook'] only after require_admin() at import.php:18 passes, so only a holder of an admin session can supply it; the candidate itself concedes this makes it hardening-level. Grep finds no assignment of is_admin anywhere in the repo, so whether a low-privilege user can become admin is unverified and outside this finding. Separately, the unauthenticated 'feed' branch at import.php:11-13 passes an attacker-supplied URL to file_get_contents with no restriction; that is a different claim and was not evaluated here.
